title: 89 Guns, 3 Arrests: Pakistani National Caught in US-Canada Gun Run
excerpt: A New York traffic stop unravels an alleged cross-border firearms scheme involving Pakistani, Canadian, and Jordanian nationals.
body:
New York State Police pulled over a vehicle in Liberty, Sullivan County, on Thursday — and what they found inside has federal prosecutors moving fast. Three men now face charges of attempting to smuggle 89 firearms, including 17 reported stolen, from the United States into Canada.

**What happened on Route 90:**
The accused are Malik Bromfield, 22, a Canadian citizen; Faizan Ali, 25, a Pakistani citizen; and Kamal Salman, 22, a citizen of Canada, the United States, and Jordan. Troopers found a suspiciously heavy suitcase that held a weapons cache, additional firearms on the back seat floor, suspected narcotics, $3,000 in cash, and an Afghan national's ID card. Investigators say the trio had left Jupiter, Florida, just the day before the arrest, with an alleged plan to traffic the weapons into Canada for profit.

**The deeper picture:**
The alleged scheme involved routing the guns through or near an Indian reservation — a corridor that First Nation chiefs say is chronically understaffed and exploited for smuggling. Ali carried an expired Pakistani driving permit issued to a different Afghan national. He also carries at least four outstanding arrest warrants in Canada, including one tied to a fatal automobile collision and another to alleged methamphetamine trafficking. The stolen firearms trace back to Texas and South Florida.

**Charges and what comes next:**
All three face counts of smuggling from the United States, unlicensed dealing in firearms, transporting stolen firearms in interstate commerce, and unlawful possession — with maximum sentences ranging from five to fifteen years. The US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York, the FBI's Hudson Valley Safe Streets Task Force, and the ATF are jointly prosecuting the case. Watch for indictment filings in White Plains federal court in the coming weeks.

sources.label: ANI / US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York (via ANI News)

nri_angle: With the alleged smuggling route passing through or near Indigenous reservation land on the US-Canada border — a corridor Indian-Americans living across the Northeast may traverse — this case is a sharp reminder that transnational criminal networks exploit the very crossings that millions of South Asians use legally every year.
author: Diaspora Desk
